own_scenes.family: Funk psicodélico y black rock: Sly, Hendrix
own_scenes.place: Costa Oeste, Memphis y Nueva York
own_scenes.desc: «El funk es blues acelerado» (Clinton). Pese a Chuck Berry, Little Richard o Bo Diddley, el rock se volvió una forma blanca y la invasión británica reforzó el mito, aunque sus grupos venían del blues negro. Hendrix y Sly lo desmontaron a finales de los sesenta, pero la industria resegregó el rock en pocos años, hasta Prince. El blues eléctrico (Muddy Waters, con su «gran caída tras el golpe del tambor») tuvo su revival ante el público blanco. En la Costa Oeste, multirracial y lejos de los problemas del Norte y del Sur, florecieron bandas mestizas (Sly, Tower of Power, Santana): la influencia del rock psicodélico convirtió el funk de un R&B salvaje en algo universal. A mediados de los setenta el black rock se convirtió en funk, porque la radio obligó a quitar los solos de guitarra; solo algunos resistieron («Who Says a Funk Band Can’t Play Rock?!» de Funkadelic, Slave, Mother’s Finest, los Isley) hasta Prince y la Black Rock Coalition de Vernon Reid (1985), y en los noventa Living Colour, Body Count, Bad Brains o Fishbone.

refs.q: Rock bands of the 1960s, both black and white, were all based in the blues. Rock bands of the 1990s, both black and white, are now based in The Funk.
refs.para: The perpetual overdose of white rock icons continues to obfuscate the rich, if misnamed, musical tradition of black rock that continues in the 1990s in the form of the black rock bands like Living Colour, Body Count, Bad Brains, Fishbone, the P-Funk All-Stars, and many others. Rock bands of the 1960s, both black and white, were all based in the blues. Rock bands of the 1990s, both black and white, are now based in The Funk. But it all comes from the same source.
refs.chapter: Cap. 9: Black rock: Givin’ It Back

refs.q: It would be the psychedelic rock influence on The Funk that served to move the style from simply a wicked brand of R&B into something universal and inclusive.
refs.para: While Hendrix remained loyal to the blues idiom throughout his career, and Sly mastered the dance music of the times, both men defied stereotypes and created organic syntheses of sound and style to produce some of the most important black rock and some of the earliest funk. It would be the psychedelic rock influence on The Funk that served to move the style from simply a wicked brand of R&B into something universal and inclusive. Uprooting racial (and musical) stereotypes with each new release, Jimi and Sly utilized the freedom inherent in rock and roll to expose thriving new visions of society—visions induced by the social revolution of the black man in America, and articulated by these black men. Symbolically, it was their time, as Jimi and Sly blew open the minds of popular music listeners and created a legacy only the funk bands have righteously followed up on.
refs.chapter: Cap. 9: Black rock: Givin’ It Back

refs.q: The “Black Rock” of the mid-1970s basically became funk.
refs.para: The “Black Rock” of the mid-1970s basically became funk. The ubiquity of radio airplay compelled black acts to dispose of their rock riffs and guitar solos, and most bands conformed. Only a few acts challenged this formula. Funkadelic took a proud stance, recording “Who Says a Funk Band Can’t Play Rock” in 1978, and a series of monster cuts from Slave, Mother’s Finest, and the Isley Brothers also made their point. It would take the rock and roll sound of Prince in 1982, and the direct political action of Vernon Reid’s Black Rock Coalition in 1985 to assert the independence and “equal rights” of black rockers to get heard, to give up The Funk, and get paid.
refs.chapter: Cap. 9: Black rock: Givin’ It Back

similar_scenes.name: Funk rock: Chili Peppers, Primus y la Black Rock Coalition
similar_scenes.book: Funk: The Music, the People, and the Rhythm of the One
similar_scenes.author: Rickey Vincent
similar_scenes.desc: A los blancos les era mucho más fácil tocar funk y grabar: Jane’s Addiction debutó con un directo, Primus de Les Claypool (devoto de Larry Graham), los Limbomaniacs con Bootsy y Maceo, Praxis. Los Red Hot Chili Peppers de Anthony Kiedis y Flea, con Freaky Styley producido por Clinton (1985), versionaron a Sly, los Meters y Stevie y llevaron a P-Funk al escenario de los Grammy de 1993; pero los creadores del funk rock, como los P-Funk All Stars, no tenían esa libertad. En Nueva York Living Colour de Vernon Reid no conseguía contrato pese a tener a Mick Jagger de fan, y Reid y Greg Tate fundaron en 1985 la Black Rock Coalition: «El rock and roll es música negra y nosotros somos sus herederos», contra el «rock de orientación apartheid». Abrió paso a Steve Coleman, Me’Shell NdegéOcello, James Blood Ulmer o el Kelvynator de Kelvyn Bell.

podcast.title: Racial Undertones in Categorization
podcast.body: The categorization of some bands as "funk rock," such as Wild Cherry, often had as much to do with the race of the musicians as with the actual musical style. "Are often categorized as a funk rock band, a label that has as much to do with their race as their music."
